Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Brotman announced the groundbreaking for Glendale’s largest affordable
  housing project, located at 515 Pioneer. The housing project will be for families and individuals
  earning between 30%-80% of the Los Angeles County Area Median Income. The housing
  project has a total of 337 units, with 245 of units for families and 92 units for seniors. He
  indicated that it would take up to three years to have all the units occupied. Brotman stated

  2
 that the city does have two additional housing projects, Harrower Village and Citrus Crossing
housing, that have already broken ground.

Councilmembers Devine and Najarian attended the Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena Airport
Authority meeting and announced that the airport will be renovating a passenger terminal.
Devine stated that the architectural design photos of the proposed airport renovation can be
seen in the Glendale City Hall lobby, and she invited the public to cast their vote on one of the
three designs. Devine nominated Tom O’Shaughnessy for the Audit Committee.

Councilmember Asatryan stated that it was brought to her attention that a year and a half ago,
Council adopted a policy regarding the appointment of mayorship. Because of the biproduct of
that policy, Asatryan was made aware that she would not be mayor during her first nor second
term. Asatryan said there has not been a councilmember in recent history who has not had the
opportunity to serve as mayor during their term. She indicated there was only one woman-
councilmember in the history of the City of Glendale who did not serve as mayor, and no one
knows the details of why. Asatryan also found out that there is a separate resolution that notes
that the appointment of the housing authority chair dictates the next mayor. She stated that
she should have been made aware regarding these policies by staff, but Asatryan found out
through a casual conversation from a friend. The meeting for the selection of the next mayor is
scheduled for April 4 and the meeting for the selection of the housing authority chair will be on
April 11. Asatryan said that unfortunately, this does not give enough time to revisit the
ordinance and asked council to consider revisiting the policy at a later date. Asatryan made it
clear she would like to be considered as the next Housing Authority Chair on April 11. She had
a meeting with the City Manager and City Attorney regarding this issue and both agreed that it
is not a fair system. Asatryan was advised that council has the authority to override the policy
for both mayor and housing authority chair selection under special circumstances. Mayor
Kassakhian stated he does not know the accuracy of the statement Asatryan provided
regarding the lack of opportunity for mayorship for two terms and asked for clarification. City
Attorney Garcia indicated based on the established rotation assuming Asatryan ran and won a
second term, she will not be able to serve as Mayor until the year 2026-2027 but it will not be
within the first two terms that she serves. Garcia will provide more information to council prior
to the April 4 Council Meeting. Councilmember Najarian indicated that this new policy was put
in place to avoid council collecting votes or having a popularity contest and that previous
councilmembers were excluded in mayorship during their term. Asatryan stated that she
appreciates the intention behind this policy, however, this has unintended consequences for
her opportunity to be selected as mayor. Asatryan added that she is the first Armenian
American woman and first immigrant woman to be elected to Glendale City Council and this
policy would prevent the city from having the first immigrant woman and first Armenian
American woman as mayor.

Councilmember Najarian announced that the Metro Board will vote on Thursday to allocate
$500K to fund a bus service for South Glendale residents to visit the Deukmejian Wilderness
Park. Najarian is a co-author of a Motion for the Metro Board to reach out to the cities in which
there are transit lines with popular stops that do not currently have amenities. This motion will
enable cities to find funding to make the bus stops and shelters as affordable and as
convenient to the riders as possible.

Mayor Kassakhian thanked the organizers of the Armenian American Museum Gala this
weekend for a well-attended event. He also thanked the people who helped get this project to
its second phase.
